# RunLocal

> RunLocal is a native Android app for offline chat, image generation, text-to-speech, audio transcription, and OCR. Install the signed ARM64 APK and browse supported downloads in Models > Add model.

RunLocal targets Android 12 (API 31) or later on ARM64. Model weights download separately. Compatibility and usable model size depend on available RAM and chipset. The app is distributed through GitHub Releases. Read the release notes for the current build status and limitations.

## Start here

- [RunLocal website](https://runlocal-android.vercel.app/): product overview and APK download. Also available on [GitHub Pages](https://07rjain.github.io/runlocal/).
- [Signed APKs and release notes](https://github.com/07rjain/runlocal/releases): use the versioned runlocal-*-arm64.apk asset and its SHA256SUMS.
- [Installation and troubleshooting](https://runlocal-android.vercel.app/support): install and update APKs, address model failures, and configure offline speech.
- [Usage and model compatibility](https://github.com/07rjain/runlocal#model-support): supported model formats and device requirements.
- [Issue tracker](https://github.com/07rjain/runlocal/issues): report reproducible bugs with app version, phone model, Android version, and model details. Remove private prompts, images, and file paths.

## Model support

- Chat supports compatible .litertlm exports through LiteRT-LM. The catalog includes Qwen3 0.6B and LFM3 1.7B. Rc10 adds CPU support for compatible single-file instruct GGUF exports through llama.cpp, including Qwen2.5 0.5B.
- Images use complete Stable Diffusion 1.x or experimental SDXL Base checkpoints on CPU. MOSS Image SFT has an experimental setup flow with a matching base and LoRA.
- Text-to-speech uses Android's offline voices or downloaded Woof, Kitten TTS 2 Pico, BlueV3 Noa, and Kokoro models. Rc10 bundles a Piper adapter that needs a compatible catalog recipe.
- Transcription uses Android's offline recognizer for microphone dictation. Rc10 lists Whisper Tiny English and Zipformer Small English for mono 16-bit PCM WAV files up to two minutes.
- OCR supports Cactus Mirage for printed Latin-script text on ARM64 and Tesseract LSTM packs for English and Hindi.
- Compatibility depends on the exact export and bundled adapter. Arbitrary ONNX graphs, .task files, general Cactus bundles, and video models require additional support.

## Setup and updates

1. Install the signed APK over an existing installation to preserve app data. Android checks signing continuity and asks the user to approve installation.
2. On rc10, open Models > Add model to browse by task and check download and memory estimates. Refresh catalog checks GitHub for new compatible listings. Supported Hugging Face links and file imports are under Other ways to add a model.
3. Select the installed chat, voice, or image model in Chat. The plus menu opens OCR and WAV transcription. Local inference is available offline after setup.
4. In rc8 or later, open Chat > history > App updates. Opt in to Include release candidates (experimental) to see newer published candidates. Earlier versions require one manual update to rc8 or later.

RunLocal uses the network for requested model downloads, catalog refreshes, and optional GitHub release checks. Chats, prompts, generated images, and model files stay local unless the user deliberately shares or exports them. RunLocal has no account, analytics SDK, cloud inference, or network speech fallback.
